insertions.question: So how do you charge Wayfair? Walk us through the revenue.
So in your, in your failed company, you're saying you couldn't find users? Or you couldn't find people to survey to get input?
Right. And they're pulling people into rooms all the time at $30 a head?
So that's how they're scaling Amazon? Through rooms of users?
So the trend on Amazon and Microsoft is more people in rooms and less AI?
So you believe in the future that rooms will get bigger, more people and prediction will just follow it?
Okay, so slow down. You've just told me that you believe your average ticket size is $400,000? Because that's my question. What do you think your average enterprise ticket price is?
Well, you think, right? So that's your supposition. So you think there's a land and expand program?

But you're still in a kind of a bit of a test track. I mean, no I admire the confidence. But the test track still is, for this company, would you agree with me, that for this company to be worth a lot of company, that software side needs to really, really grow?

I'm not trying... You're not on trial. What I'm trying to do is ask where you are because you're asking us for money. Because there's a big difference between saying, I think people are going to spend 400 grand or 50 grand, or whether you've done it not. That's like, that's a very big distance, right?
Let me just parrot back your number to you right. So at the end of 2019, about $2 million will be enterprise revenue, right?

omitted_candidates.text: Can you give us an example of how that works?
Who do you see as your most direct competitors?
So this new company is solving a problem that you were experiencing with your old company?
What's the size of the addressable market, would you say?
How do you price your enterprise product?
And what are you telling your investors for by the end of 2019 your sales are going to be?
And how much of that is your front end vs your back end?
What do you think the valuation is?
